title: Aerial photo land-use sheets with a colour key
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y5 lesson 15 (Aerial photo land-use sheets with a colour key (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 15: How is land used? Reading aerial images. To understand how land is used in the UK and how to identify land use on aerial images

model.title: What is this land used for?

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Long thin green and brown strips beside houses: allotments

questions.q: Is a housing estate urban or rural?
questions.model: A housing estate has many houses close together. That is a built-up area. So it is urban.

questions.a: Growing your own fruit and vegetables

questions.q: What is most UK land used for?
On the three aerial photo sheets, colour-code the land use (key given) and write the main land use for each photo with a reason.
questions.a: Accurate colour-coding and a reason for each, e.g. photo B is arable because of large brown and yellow fields
questions.model: Teacher colour-codes the first quarter of photo A.

questions.q: Write which land use you see most near your home and why.
questions.a: A sensible answer using urban or rural

questions.q: Why might people disagree about building houses on farmland?
questions.a: Homes are needed, but farmland grows food and countryside is lost

questions.q: Big question: what colour would you see most?
questions.a: Green and brown: most UK land is farmland
